links.outcome: Top-3 differential diagnosis accuracy of multimodal LLMs vs neuroradiologists on neuroradiology quiz cases
links.effect: LLM top-3 accuracy 29.9% to 49.4% versus radiologists 80.3% and 68.3% (P < 0.001); only 29.4% (118 of 401) of LLM analyses acceptable; hallucinations in 4.5% (18 of 401).
links.quote: Top-3 accuracy (i.e., correct answers present among top-3 differential diagnoses) of LLMs ranged from 29.9% (120 of 401) to 49.4% (198 of 401, obtained with GPT-4V in the T1 setting), while radiologists achieved 80.3% (322 of 401) and 68.3% (274 of 401), respectively (P < 0.001).

links.outcome: LLM performance and reasoning when textual clinical history was absent, and across temperature settings
links.effect: GPT-4V (T1) identified both lesion location and imaging findings in 30.7% (123 of 401) and 12.9% (16 of 124) of cases without textual clinical history; performance declined without clinical history text.
links.quote: LLMs remarkably underperformed compared with neuroradiologists and showed unsatisfactory reasoning for their differential diagnoses, with performance declining further in cases without textual input of clinical history.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic accuracy, reasoning, and hallucination rates of several multimodal LLMs against human radiologists on neuroradiology cases without evaluating a deployment guardrail.
